emergency_assistant_system_prompt: You are CPR Coach, a calm conversational emergency voice assistant like Siri. You help with CPR and cardiac emergencies. Answer the user's specific question in natural spoken language (2–4 sentences). Remember earlier turns in this conversation. Ground answers in the CPR reference material provided each turn. Never cite AHA, Red Cross, or other certifying organizations by name. Always tell users to call 911 or local emergency services in true emergencies — never say to skip calling. Never diagnose. Speak directly to the user. Be reassuring but clear and urgent when lives may be at risk.
voice_llm_empty: I didn't catch that. Please try again.
voice_opener_question_2: Here's what you need to know.
voice_opener_calm_2: You're doing the right thing by asking.
voice_reassure_1: Keep going — any CPR is better than none.
voice_reassure_2: You're helping give them the best chance.

voice_live_elbows: Lock your elbows straight — use your body weight, not just your arms.
voice_live_camera: Try to keep the camera steady so I can coach your form better.
guided_opening: Hi, this is CPR Coach, I'm going to guide you step by step. First: Is this a medical emergency right now? Say yes or no.
guided_confirm_emergency_retry: I need to know — is someone seriously hurt, unconscious, or not breathing? Say yes if this is an emergency.
guided_not_emergency: Understood. If anything changes, call 911 immediately. You can tap Voice AI again anytime. Take care.
guided_ask_age: Thank you. How old is the person? Say infant, child, or adult.
guided_ask_age_retry: Please say infant for a baby, child for someone young, or adult.
guided_scene_safe: Before you approach — make sure the scene is safe for you. When you are with the person, say ready.
guided_check_responsive: Go to the person now. Tap their shoulder firmly and shout 'Are you okay!'. Are they responding at all — any movement or answer?
guided_check_responsive_retry: After tapping and shouting — are they responding? Say yes if they move or answer, no if there is no response.
guided_check_breathing: Look at their chest for no more than ten seconds. Are they breathing normally? Remember — gasping is not normal breathing.
guided_check_breathing_responsive: They respond — good. Now look at their chest for ten seconds. Are they breathing normally?
guided_check_breathing_retry: Watch their chest. Are they breathing normally? Say yes, no, or not sure.
guided_call911_urgent: They need help now. Call 911 or your local emergency number immediately. Put your phone on speaker. Tell me when you have called.
guided_call911_worsening: Call 911 right now — their breathing is not normal. Put the phone on speaker and tell me when you have called.
guided_confirm_911: Have you called 911 or emergency services? Say yes when you are on the line or have called.
guided_confirm_911_retry: It is critical to call 911 now. Say yes once you have called or are on the phone with them.
guided_call911_now: Please call 911 now. Put your phone on speaker so I can keep guiding you. Tell me when you have called.
guided_get_aed: Good. If anyone else is nearby, tell them to find an AED. When you are ready to start CPR, say ready.
guided_start_cpr_adult: Place the heel of your hand on the center of the chest. Push hard and fast — at least two inches deep, one hundred to one twenty compressions per minute. Allow full chest recoil. Start compressions now. Say ready when you begin.
guided_start_cpr_child: For a child, place one or two hands on the center of the chest. Push about two inches deep at one hundred to one twenty per minute. Start compressions now. Say ready when you begin.
guided_start_cpr_infant: For an infant, use two fingers on the center of the chest. Push about one and a half inches deep at one hundred to one twenty per minute. Start compressions now. Say ready when you begin.
guided_cpr_active: You are doing great — keep going. Do not stop compressions unless they become responsive and breathe normally.
guided_push_now: Start pushing on the chest now — hard and fast. I am here with you.
guided_keep_going: Keep going — do not stop. You are giving them the best chance.
guided_good_cpr: Good compressions — keep that rhythm and depth.
guided_and_continue: Keep compressing — you are doing the right thing.
guided_breathing_ok: They are breathing. Place them in the recovery position on their side, monitor them closely, and call 911 if they get worse. I will stay with you — tell me if anything changes.
guided_recovery_check: If they are breathing and responsive, place them on their side in the recovery position. Monitor them until EMS arrives. Tell me if anything changes.
guided_recovery_stay: Stay with them. Watch their breathing and be ready to start CPR again if they become unresponsive. EMS is on the way.
guided_unclear_help: I did not catch that. Please answer with yes or no, or tell me infant, child, or adult.

actionfix_correct: Great compressions. Keep this rhythm and depth.
actionfix_overlap_hands: Stack your hands directly on top of each other, fingers interlaced.
actionfix_clenching_hands: Open your fingers. Press with the heel of your palm, not a fist.
actionfix_single_hand: Use both hands — place one on top of the other on the chest center.
actionfix_bending_arms: Lock your elbows straight and press from your shoulders.
actionfix_tilting_arms: Bring your shoulders directly above your hands and press straight down.
actionfix_jump_pressing: Stay steady — compress with your arms, do not bounce your whole body.
actionfix_squatting: Kneel beside the patient instead of squatting for better leverage.
actionfix_standing: Kneel down beside the patient and lean over the chest.
actionfix_insufficient_pressing: Push deeper — compress at least 5 centimeters.
actionfix_slow_frequency: Compress faster — aim for 100 to 120 per minute.
actionfix_excessive_pressing: Ease the depth slightly — no more than 6 centimeters.
actionfix_random_position_pressing: Keep your hands fixed on one spot in the center of the chest.

chatcpr_system_prompt: You are ChatCPR, an advanced CPR and emergency cardiovascular care assistant for Vision CPR Coach. You are grounded in national and international CPR training standards and evidence-based resuscitation practice. RULES: Give accurate, detailed, professional-level answers suitable for someone studying CPR certification. Use the CPR reference snippets provided each turn — do not invent drug doses, protocols, or diagnoses. Never cite AHA, Red Cross, or other certifying organizations by name in your replies. For emergencies, always tell the user to call local emergency services first. Never diagnose medical conditions or tell users to skip calling EMS. Reference live compression metrics and joint analysis when provided. Use clear paragraphs. Plain text only — no markdown. This is educational coaching, not a substitute for certified training or professional medical care.
emergency_openrouter_system_prompt: You are CPR Coach on a live emergency phone call. The user has completed the full guided setup and is now performing CPR. RULES: Answer in natural spoken language — 2 to 4 short sentences, calm and direct like a dispatcher. Plain text only. No markdown or organization names. Use the CPR reference and live metrics when provided. Reinforce continuing compressions unless the victim is clearly responsive and breathing normally. Never diagnose. Match the same reassuring tone as the guided steps before.
progress_analysis_system_prompt: You are CPR Coach analytics. Summarize practice session metrics for the rescuer. Be specific, calm, and actionable. Plain text only.
llm_reply_language: IMPORTANT: Reply only in %@. Use natural, fluent %@ for all coaching, explanations, and emergency guidance.
